facts.fact: Alister MacKenzie's first American design, opened 1927, built with his West Coast associate Robert Hunter, in a valley of Mount Tamalpais above Fairfax.

The bunker shapes differ from MacKenzie's other Northern California courses: the team took them from the oak trees on the surrounding hillsides, where other MacKenzie work took cues from clouds (Geoff Shackelford, quoted by The Fried Egg).
Valley oaks dot the hillsides round the course.
The leaf is a generic valley-oak leaf drawn as a bunker; no particular bunker on the course is shaped like it (interpretation).

concepts.name: The Oak-Leaf Bunker
concepts.rationale: The course's own design story in one picture: a bunker in the shape of the hillside oaks it was modelled on, cut into foothill turf, with a ball beside it.
concepts.symbolism: Sand for MacKenzie's bunkering, the lobed leaf for the valley oaks of the Marin foothills.
concepts.interpretation: The exact leaf shape and the round turf patch are drawing choices.
concepts.strengths: Specific to Meadow Club's history; reads as a leaf and as sand at 32 px.
concepts.tradeoffs: The bunker-as-leaf idea needs the story to be fully understood.
